title: Further Reduction of the Bonus Ledger Basis by Card Standing
content:
How far the bonus ledger basis of a savings or money market account of Savings & Money Market Accounts is further reduced turns on the owner's standing under Personal Credit Cards: the card balance owed, and the card payments posted in the three calendar months ending on the review date.

| Card balance owed | Card payments in the three calendar months ending on the review date | The further reduction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1500.00 USD or less | at least 1000.00 USD | none is made, and the bonus ledger basis itself stands as the figure to be capped |
| more than 1500.00 USD, no more than 4000.00 USD | at least 1000.00 USD | the withdrawals posted in the one calendar month ending on the review date |
| more than 4000.00 USD | any | the withdrawals posted in the three calendar months ending on the review date |
| any | below 1000.00 USD | the withdrawals posted in the three calendar months ending on the review date |

### Where the cap falls

In every branch the tier's relationship bonus balance cap is applied after that further reduction, never before it. The order is fixed: the further reduction is taken off the bonus ledger basis first, the result is taken as no less than zero, and only then is the cap applied to what remains.

### A worked case on hypothetical inputs

Take a savings account whose bonus ledger basis is 28000.00 USD, whose withdrawals come to 900.00 USD in the one calendar month ending on the review date and 4300.00 USD in the three calendar months ending on that date, and take a hypothetical relationship bonus balance cap of 30000.00 USD.

Where the owner's card owes 1200.00 USD and card payments of 1500.00 USD posted in the window, no further reduction is made and the figure to be capped is 28000.00 USD.

Where the card owes 3000.00 USD and those card payments still reach 1000.00 USD, the further reduction is 900.00 USD, giving 27100.00 USD to be capped.

Where the card owes 5000.00 USD, or the card payments come to 800.00 USD, the further reduction is 4300.00 USD, giving 23700.00 USD to be capped.

### Boundary figures

A card balance owed of exactly 1500.00 USD falls in the first branch; 1500.01 USD falls in the second so long as it is no more than 4000.00 USD; 4000.01 USD falls in the third. Card payments of exactly 1000.00 USD satisfy the payment condition of the first two branches.
